# Sonosphere developer documentation

> Sonosphere is a scrobbling service and music community. It exposes Last.fm-compatible and ListenBrainz-compatible APIs, plus public now-playing snapshots and streams.

## Documentation

- [Developer API](https://sonosphere.fm/developers): Authentication, signing, supported methods and examples.
- [ListenBrainz API](https://sonosphere.fm/developers#listenbrainz): Listen submission, feedback, social endpoints and statistics.
- [Public now-playing API](https://sonosphere.fm/developers#public-now-playing): JSON snapshots, Server-Sent Events and WebSockets.
- [Applications](https://sonosphere.fm/settings/applications): Create API keys, shared secrets and ListenBrainz tokens (login required).
- [Scrobbling help](https://sonosphere.fm/help): Connect a music player.

## Last.fm-compatible API

Root URL: https://sonosphere.fm/2.0/

Send method, api_key and parameters as a query string for reads or a form-encoded POST for writes. Add format=json for JSON; XML is the default. Create an API key and shared secret in Settings > Applications.

### Authentication

- Web: send the user to https://sonosphere.fm/api/auth?api_key=KEY&cb=URL. The callback receives ?token=TOKEN; exchange it with auth.getSession within an hour. Without cb, the saved callback is used. A supplied cb must be on the same site as the saved callback.
- Desktop: call auth.getToken, send the user to https://sonosphere.fm/api/auth?api_key=KEY&token=TOKEN, then call auth.getSession.
- Scripts: POST auth.getMobileSession with username and password.

All three auth methods are signed. Session keys do not expire. Authenticated methods use the session key as sk.

### Signing

Sort all parameters except format and callback by name. Concatenate each name and value without separators, append the shared secret, and send the MD5 hex digest as api_sig.

### Examples

```sh
# Scrobble (macOS: replace md5sum | cut -d' ' -f1 with md5 -q)
KEY=your_api_key; SECRET=your_shared_secret; SK=session_key; TS=$(date +%s)
SIG=$(printf 'api_key%sartistGlass Harbormethodtrack.scrobblesk%stimestamp%strackWhen the Echoes Come%s' \
  "$KEY" "$SK" "$TS" "$SECRET" | md5sum | cut -d' ' -f1)
curl -X POST https://sonosphere.fm/2.0/ -d method=track.scrobble -d api_key=$KEY -d sk=$SK -d timestamp=$TS \
  --data-urlencode "artist=Glass Harbor" --data-urlencode "track=When the Echoes Come" -d api_sig=$SIG -d format=json

# Read recent tracks
curl "https://sonosphere.fm/2.0/?method=user.getRecentTracks&user=USERNAME&api_key=KEY&format=json"
```

Batch scrobbles use indexed parameters such as artist[0] and track[0], up to 50 scrobbles per call.

### Supported methods

- Auth: auth.getToken, auth.getSession, auth.getMobileSession.
- Track: track.scrobble, track.updateNowPlaying, track.love, track.unlove, track.getInfo, track.getSimilar, track.getTopTags, track.search, track.addTags, track.removeTag.
- Artist: artist.getInfo, artist.getTopTracks, artist.getTopAlbums, artist.getSimilar, artist.getTopTags, artist.search, artist.addTags, artist.removeTag.
- Album: album.getInfo, album.getTopTags, album.search, album.addTags, album.removeTag.
- User: user.getInfo, user.getRecentTracks, user.getTopArtists, user.getTopAlbums, user.getTopTracks, user.getLovedTracks, user.getFriends, user.getTopTags.
- Tag: tag.getInfo, tag.getTopArtists, tag.getTopTracks, tag.getTopAlbums.
- Chart: chart.getTopArtists, chart.getTopTracks, chart.getTopTags.

### Errors

JSON failures return {"error": CODE, "message": "..."}. Codes: 3 invalid method, 4 authentication failed, 6 invalid parameters, 9 invalid session, 10 invalid API key, 13 invalid signature, 14 unauthorised token.

## ListenBrainz-compatible API

Root URL: https://sonosphere.fm/1/

Use the same paths, request bodies and responses as ListenBrainz. Configure clients and libraries with https://sonosphere.fm as the server URL.

Users create a token in Settings > Applications. Send it as Authorization: Token TOKEN. Reads do not need a token, except to see your own private listening.

Errors return {"code": 400, "error": "..."} with the matching HTTP status. Statistics with nothing to show return 204. The rate limit is 100 requests per 10 seconds per address, reported in X-RateLimit-* headers.

recording_msid values are Sonosphere-local identifiers. A recording_mbid is known once a client has sent it with a listen. Statistics are live, use UTC, and support all ranges from this_week to all_time.

### Examples

```sh
# Submit a listen
curl -X POST https://sonosphere.fm/1/submit-listens \
  -H "Authorization: Token TOKEN" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"listen_type": "single", "payload": [{"listened_at": '$(date +%s)',
       "track_metadata": {"artist_name": "Glass Harbor", "track_name": "When the Echoes Come"}}]}'

# Read listens
curl "https://sonosphere.fm/1/user/USERNAME/listens?count=10"
```

### Supported endpoints (relative to /1/)

- Auth: GET validate-token.
- Listens: POST submit-listens; POST delete-listen; GET user/{user}/listens; GET user/{user}/listen-count; GET user/{user}/playing-now; GET and POST latest-import.
- Feedback: POST feedback/recording-feedback; GET feedback/user/{user}/get-feedback; GET and POST feedback/user/{user}/get-feedback-for-recordings; GET feedback/recording/{msid}/get-feedback; GET feedback/recording/{mbid}/get-feedback-mbid.
- Social: GET user/{user}/followers; GET user/{user}/following; POST user/{user}/follow; POST user/{user}/unfollow; GET user/{user}/similar-users; GET user/{user}/similar-to/{other}; GET user/{user}/services; GET search/users.
- User statistics: GET stats/user/{user}/artists, releases, release-groups, recordings, listening-activity, daily-activity (each suffix is a separate endpoint).
- Site statistics: GET stats/sitewide/artists, releases, release-groups, recordings (each suffix is a separate endpoint).
- Listeners: GET stats/artist/{mbid}/listeners; GET stats/release-group/{mbid}/listeners.

Playlists, recommendations, radio, metadata lookups and data dumps are not available.

## Public now-playing API

No key, signature or login is required. Cross-origin requests are allowed.

- JSON snapshot: GET https://sonosphere.fm/api/user/nowplaying?name=USERNAME
- Server-Sent Events: GET https://sonosphere.fm/api/user/nowplaying/stream?name=USERNAME
- WebSocket: wss://sonosphere.fm/api/user/nowplaying/ws?name=USERNAME

### Snapshot payload

```json
{
  "t": "nowplaying",
  "user": { "username": "USERNAME" },
  "nowPlaying": {
    "trackId": 123,
    "title": "When the Echoes Come",
    "artist": "Glass Harbor",
    "album": "Night Signals",
    "duration": 210,
    "startedAt": 1795219200,
    "imageUrl": "https://sonosphere.fm/api/image/IMAGE_ID"
  }
}
```

nowPlaying is null when nothing is playing. album and imageUrl can be null. duration is in seconds (0 if unknown). startedAt is the Unix time of the latest update, not a playback position.

Streams send the current state on connection and a snapshot on every change. Past events are not replayed. If listening becomes private or the account goes away, streams send unavailable and close; do not reconnect after that event. WebSockets send {"t":"ping"} every 15 seconds; no reply is needed.

Errors: 400 bad name, 403 private listening, 404 unknown user, 429 rate limited (with Retry-After). Spotify listening is checked about once a minute, so changes can take that long to appear.

### Server-Sent Events example

```js
const url = new URL("https://sonosphere.fm/api/user/nowplaying/stream");
url.searchParams.set("name", "USERNAME");
const stream = new EventSource(url);
stream.addEventListener("nowplaying", e => {
  const { nowPlaying } = JSON.parse(e.data);
  label.textContent = nowPlaying ? nowPlaying.artist + " - " + nowPlaying.title : "Not listening";
});
stream.addEventListener("unavailable", () => stream.close());
```
